audit.why: 49.11% over 1067 games. Levels 2-5 are a clean gate-Q window against a pre-Rylai's Vladimir, level 6 hands him Hemoplague, and two items make him unkillable for a zero-defence caster.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four stages disagree with their captions. whys[3] says 'You out-trade a pre-Rylai Vlad all day' under a Skill 4-5; whys[4] says 'Level 6 flips toward Vlad' under a Skill level 6; whys[5] says the first item 'still trades' under a Jayce stage; and late says 'He out-scales me hard' under a Jayce 2+ items.
audit.why: The chart never lets Vladimir own a single stage even though the page says he takes the lane from 6 onward. Packet reference chart Skill|Jayce|Jayce|Jayce|Vladimir|Skill|Vladimir matches every caption.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Skill, Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Vladimir, Skill, Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is described only as poke. Riot's text ends 'but can be blocked by enemy units' — minions eat it. And Sanguine Pool's untargetability is called open-ended when it is exactly 2 seconds on a 28/25/22/19/16s cooldown.
audit.why: Standing behind your own minion wave turns his entire mid-range poke tool off, which is real, free counterplay the page never offers. And the pool being 2 seconds against a 28-second cooldown reframes it: baiting it does not buy you a moment, it buys you almost half a minute.
audit.corrected: The unit-block on Tides of Blood stated in late; the 2s/28s numbers stated in mid and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds call anywhere despite every one of his damage tools healing him.
audit.why: Transfusion heals on a 9s cooldown falling to 4.6s, and Hemoplague heals him for each champion hit. Flagged missing for this matchup. Anti-heal is the buy that keeps the 4-5 window open past his first item.

edits.before: This is my window. Through 4-5 I have both forms and he still lacks Rylai's and the cooldowns to fight back, so I keep tilting the poke war — gate-Q his step-ups, and when he commits to a Transfusion cycle on the wave I all-in: Cannon-Q to apply the swap-shred, swap to Hammer, To-the-Skies leap in, Thundering Blow to knock him back and interrupt, Lightning Field to finish. The one rule is Sanguine Pool: if it is up I give nothing, because it eats my whole combo and makes him untargetable mid-shred. Level 6 is where it levels off — my R is just the stance-swap I already had, while Hemoplague is a real burst-and-heal amp, so this is the stage he claws back even.
edits.after: This is my window. Through 4-5 I have both forms and he still lacks Rylai's and the cooldowns to fight back, so I keep tilting the poke war — gate-Q his step-ups, and when he commits to a Transfusion cycle on the wave I all-in: Cannon-Q for the swap-shred, swap to Hammer, To-the-Skies leap in, Thundering Blow to knock him back, Lightning Field to finish. The one rule is Sanguine Pool: it is 28s at rank 1 and only 2 seconds of untargetability, so bait it and the rest of that half-minute is mine. Transfusion heals every 9s, so Grievous Wounds earns its slot. Level 6 levels off — my R is only the stance-swap while Hemoplague amps his burst and heals him off it.

edits.before: He out-scales me hard. By two items a full-AP Vlad pools my burst on reaction, pokes me with Tides of Blood, and Hemoplague amps a Transfusion drain that out-sustains anything I bring — my squishy, defenseless frame just melts in the extended fight I can no longer win. There is no straight 1v1 for me here, so everything I do has to bank before this point: take the plates, take the health lead, end the lane in the first three buys. If it goes long I stop dueling him, hold back and chip with Cannon-Q poke from max range, and let my team handle the unkillable drain-mage he becomes.
edits.after: He out-scales me hard. Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units, though: standing behind my own minions eats it outright. There is no straight 1v1 for me here, so everything banks before this point — take the plates, take the health lead, end the lane in the first three buys. If it goes long I chip with Cannon-Q from max range and let my team handle the drain-mage.

edits.before: Bait Sanguine Pool with a half-commit, then full-combo Cannon-Q swap-shred into Hammer To-the-Skies, Thundering Blow and Lightning Field while the pool is on its long cooldown
edits.after: Bait Sanguine Pool with a half-commit — it is only 2s of untargetability on a 28s cooldown — then full-combo Cannon-Q swap-shred into Hammer To-the-Skies, Thundering Blow and Lightning Field

notes: Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units — your own minion wave turns off his mid-range poke, and the page never said so. Sanguine Pool is 2 seconds of untargetability on a 28s rank-1 cooldown, which is what makes baiting it worth doing. 'Hit Sanguine Pool' and 'Sanguine Pool's' were flagged as suspect ability names in the packet; both are false positives — the name is correct in each case.
